report: Aus der Vordiagnostik [DATE] bek. und hierzu progrediente, medial betonte Pangonarthrose mit flächig vollschichtiger Chondropathie beider Gelenkpartner in der Belastungszone mit Ausdünnung und teils Mehrsklerosierierung der subchondralen Kortikalis sowie progredienter ausgedehnter subchondraler Reizreaktion femorotibial. Oberflächliche Chondropathie auch in den anderen Gelenkkompartimenten ohne tiefergreifende Läsion. Außenmeniskus gering mukoid ohne Riss. Innenmeniskus bei mukoider Vorschädigung mit Lappenriss in der Pars intermedia und umgeschlagenen Anteil auf die Meniskussubstanz parafemoral (5/20). Medial ausgeprägte Reizzustand des Kapselbandapparates. VKB gering mukoid. Ansonsten Bandapparat regelrecht. Kleine Plica mediopatellaris. Geringer Gelenkerguss, dtl. chron. Reizsynovialitis, minimal flüssigkeitsgefüllte Baker-Zyste.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Lateral knee pain.
Comparison: Right knee radiograph [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.2 Tesla open system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Small leaking Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear involving the body, posterior horn and posterior root, noting a complete radial tear at the posterior root. Moderate meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss/fissuring and associated subchondral signal changes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint in the lateral joint line.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss throughout the patella with areas of full-thickness loss at the median ridge and medial facet with associated subchondral signal changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon. Stripping of the prepatellar quadriceps continuation. Prepatellar bursitis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 12 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body, posterior horn and posterior root. Dominant complete radial component at the posterior root. Moderate meniscal extrusion.
2.	Mild-to-moderate tricompartmental osteoarthritis. Moderate knee joint effusion.
3.	Small leaking Baker's cyst.
4.	Prepatellar bursitis.

Indication: Medial joint pain for 20 years, no known cause. No surgical history.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal tendinosis with insertional enthesopathy.

1. Tricompartmental chondrosis, moderate in the medial compartment.

2. No acute osseous, ligamentous or meniscal injury.

- The study reveals severe full thickness cartilage degeneration of medial tibial plateau and medial femoral condyle, measured about 2.2 cm and 2.3 cm in length, respectively. Thin cartilage degeneration with focal delamination tear of anterior aspect of lateral tibial plateau, measured about intact8 cm in length. There are bilateral marginal osteophytes and no subchondral bone change. The thin cartilage degeneration with fissuring surface of medial and lateral side of patella and trochlea and narrowing of patellofemoral joint is noted. Overall findings are suggested degenerative change of knee. 
 - There are multiple loose bodies which one ossified lesion at medial side of capsule, measured about 1.2 cm, and three calcified lesions at anteromedial, posteromedial and posterosuperior medial side of capsule are seen, measured up to intact8 cm. 
  
 Central supporting system  
 - Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): There is enlarged and mucoid degenerative change is noted.  
 - Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  
 - No evidence of anterior tibial translation is noted.  
  
 Medial compartment  
 - Medial meniscus: Mild bulging with horizontal tear at body and posterior horn and radial tear at posterior horn and posterior root are noted. 
 - Medial collateral ligament: Intact. 
 - Medial tibial plateau: Normal.  
 - Medial femoral condyle: Normal.  
  
 Lateral compartment  
 - Lateral meniscus: Myxoid degenerative change without definite tear. 
 - Iliotibial band: Normal.  
 - Lateral collateral ligament: Mild increased SI without definite tear.  
 - Popliteus tendon: Increased SI with minimal fluid. 
 - Popliteofibular ligament: Normal.  
 - Biceps femoris tendon : Preserved.  
 - Lateral tibial plateau: Normal.  
 - Lateral femoral condyle: Normal.  
  
 Patellofemoral compartment  
 - Quadriceps tendon: Normal.  
 - Patellar tendon: Normal with mild subcutaneous edema.  
 - Medial patellar retinaculum:Normal. 
 - Lateral patellar retinaculum: Normal.  
  
 Others  
 - Effusion within tibiofemoral joint and patellofemoral jont extending along suprapatellar bursa is observed. Associated thickening of synovial lining along these sites are noted; likely synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis.  
 - Muscle bulks grade I at tibialis anterior, fibularis longus, extensor digitorum longus and grade II of vartus muscles are noted. 
 - Neurovascular bundles are intact.   - Degenerative change of right knee. 
 - Stained of lateral collateral ligament and popliteal tendon. 
 - Effusion within tibiofemoral joint and patellofemoral jont extending along suprapatellar bursa associated thickening of synovial lining along these sites; likely synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis.

Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.

aproximadamente 6 x 13 mm en sus ejes mediolateral y anteroposterior, sin edema óseo.
Finas úlceras condrales de espesor parcial de platillo tibial lateral.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial medial y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras
condrales de espesor total de la faceta lateral de la rótula con cambios óseos secundarios.

[DATE]: MR Knie Rechts 15ch AA: Klinische inlichtingen: Zie gescande aanvraag Diagnostische vraagstelling: Zie gescande aanvraag Bevindingen: Matig tot gevorderd mediaal femorotibiaal kraakbeenlijden, met quasi volledig kraakbeenverlies op het dragende deel van de mediale femorale condyl en het tibiaplateau, gepaard gaand met kleine subchondrale geode's, marginale osteofytose. Degeneratief voorkomen mediale meniscus met onregelmatige aflijning, echter zonder duidelijke scheur . Beginnend tot matig lateraal femorotibiaal kraakbeenlijden, met oppervlakkige en diepe fissuren. Matige opzetting van suprapatellaire recessus. Beginnend tot matig femoropatellair kraakbeenlijden met oppervlakkige en diepe fissuren. Popliteale cyste, met craniocaudale as 6\~cm. Normaal voorkomen verschillende pezen. Besluit: Beginnende gonartrose van de rechterknie met beginnend tot matig tot gevorderd kraakbeenlijden graad 2, 3 en 4, in alle 3 compartimenten, op heden met matige hydrops.

Mediales Kompartiment:
Osteophytäre Anbauten an der medialen Femurcondyle. Vollständig fehlender Knorpelbesatz in der Belastungszone an der medialen Femurcondyle sowie fokal vollschichtige Knorpeldefekte in der tibialen Belastungszone mit angrenzend deutlichem subchondralem Knochenödem. Geringes subchondrales Knochenödem an der medialen Femurcondyle. Komplexe Rissbildung mit kleiner Lappenkomponente in der Pars intermedia und dem Hinterhorn des Innenmeniskus mit radiärer und vertikaler Komponente (Serie 3/ Image 116, Serie 4/ Image 24) bei deutlicher mukoider Auffaserung. Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Osteophytäre Anbuaten an der lateralen Femurcondyle. Fokal vollschichtiger 5 x 6 mm messender Knorpeldefekt in der dorsalen Belastungszone der lateralen Femurcondyle mit geringem angrenzendem subchondralem Knochenödem (Serie 4/ Image 25). Geringe mukoide Degeneration im Außenmeniskushinterhorn. Intaktes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:
Geringe Lateralisierung der Patella. Oberflächliche Knorpelirregularitäten retropatellar und trochleär mit teils auch tieferen Einrissen und subchondraler Zystenbildung an der lateralen Patellafacette sowie an der Trochlea beidseits (Serie 3/ Image 38). Regelrechte Darstellung der Quadrizeps- und Patellarsehne. Regelrechte Darstellung des Hoffa`schen Fettkörpers.

Kreuzbänder:
Intakte Kreuzbänder.

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Geringer Gelenkerguss mit verdickter Synovia und synovialen Proliferationen. Flüssigkeitsgefüllte Baker-Zyste.

Findings: There is a moderate knee effusion. There is degenerate tearing of the body of medial meniscus which is seen to be extruded from the joint. Normal lateral meniscus.  
Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is complete loss of the medial compartment articular cartilage with underlying medial femoral and tibial condylar marrow edema. The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Minor subchondral bony change is noted in the lateral patellar facet. The patellofemoral articular cartilage is however well preserved.  
Conclusion: Severe medial compartment OA change with degenerate tearing and extrusion of the medial meniscal body.
